source_reports.citation: Rao, A.R., 2006, Flood frequency relationships for Indiana: Joint Transportation Research Program, Purdue University, Final Report FHWA/IN/JTRP-2005/18, SPR-2858 (March 2006)

Knipe, David, and Rao, A.R., 2005, Estimation of peak discharges of Indiana streams by using log Pearson (III) distribution: Joint Transportation Research Program, Purdue University, Interim Report No. 1, FHWA/IN/JTRP-2005/1 (May 2005)

notes: Rao (March 2006), Chapter 3: GLS equations at 6 AEPs in 8 regions from 223 gages, whose at-site quantiles are Bulletin 17B LP3 fits from PEAKFQ. Knipe and Rao (May 2005) prints the same tables (4.4-4.12), cell for cell, and adds the worked examples and the gage lists (Appendixes A and B). NSS's citation says 2005 and 14 p.; the report is dated March 2006 and its documentation page gives 138 pages. Every constant, exponent and range equals NSS, and the constant is printed, so intercept = log10(C). NSS's HIGHREG limit of 1005-1012, on each region's 10 percent equation only, is the same in all 8 regions, so it selects nothing and the report does not have it: it is left out. Out of scope: Chapters 4-6's L-moment and GLS relations for PT3, GEV and L-moment LP3 quantiles (Tables 4.2.1-4.2.2, 5.2.3-5.2.9, 5.3.1-5.3.2). They are alternatives, partly on 6 merged regions; NSS does not serve them, and conclusion 2 (p. 136) sends users who must use LP3 to Chapter 3. Error statistics: 'Avg Model Error' is the model error variance, and %Error is that alone by equation 3.5.1, not a standard error of prediction, so sep_log is not stored. Table 3.7.2 calls it average model error. %Error reproduces from the variance at all 48 equations. 'Avg Eq YOR' is equivalent_years. Neither report prints a covariance or AVP, so these equations give no interval. Equation 3.5.9 needs the covariance. Examples 1 and 3 print limits, called 95 percent but headed 0.05 and 0.95: they are 90 percent limits, since at 95 percent they imply a prediction variance below the model error variance. At 90 percent they imply xUx of about 0.0015-0.004. Worked examples 1, 2 and 3 reproduce within the rounding of the printed coefficients and flows. Neither report prints regression flows by gage. Table 3.7.1's percent errors at 44 gages reproduce within the rounding of the inputs, and Table 3.7.2's column 3 regional mean errors over all 223 gages reproduce within 0.1 percentage point, except region 3 at 24.4 against 25.0, unexplained. Inconsistencies in the report, kept as printed unless stated: Table 3.5.1 lists 22 gages for region 7, where Appendix A lists 21 and the text's total of 223 needs 21, so n_sites is 21; p. 52's account of region 7's split sample implies 20. Table 3.5.10's region 3 drainage-area maximum of 284 mi2 is also NSS's, but Appendix A has 03303000 at 476 mi2 in region 3, and the next largest is 03277000 at 248 mi2. StreamStats gives 03303000 a CONTDA of 290 mi2, so 284 may be its effective area, but using 284 moves region 3's mean error further from Table 3.7.2 (21.9 against 25.0, where 476 gives 24.4), so this is unsettled. Region 1's slope maximum of 79 is 79.5 at 03378590. The model error variances of region 5 at 0.5 percent (0.020) and region 7 at 1 percent (0.034) break their regions' trends, but %Error and Table 3.7.2 agree with them. Region selection: the report maps regions by 14-digit HUC (Figure 3.1.2 and Knipe and Rao's Appendix D, on a CD-ROM not available here) and says the location of the point of discharge determination selects the equation (Knipe and Rao, Example 2), not an area weighting. flowfreq's estimate_at_site weights by NSS's percent_weight instead, so a basin crossing a region boundary does not follow the report's rule: at 03364500 (region 3 in Appendix A, HIGHREG 1007, 15 percent of its area in region 3), Q100 is 10,614 cfs area-weighted and 17,827 cfs on region 3 alone, against 13,100 cfs at-site. %W and %U are from 1990s NLCD, codes 11, 12, 91, 92 and 21, 22, 23; Knipe and Rao's example counts 11, 91 and 92. Knipe and Rao head the drainage area ContDA and EffDA, net of noncontributing area, which is NSS's CONTDA.
